<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 />to regard them as representing the original stem (with two radicals), and the forms with the second radical repeated as subsequently developed from the monosyllabic stem.<ref>So (partly following Ewald and Böttcher) A. Müller, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxiii. p. 698 ff.; Stade, ''Lehrbuch'', {{GHGpar|385|b}}, c; Nöldeke, and more recently Wellhausen, ‘''Ueber einige Arten schwacher Verba im Hebr.''’ (''Skizzen u. Vorarb.'' vi. 250 ff.). Against Böttcher see M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxxv. 330 ff., and Brockelmann, as above.</ref> The appearance of a general contraction of triliteral stems is due to the fact that in biliteral forms the second radical regularly receives {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} before afformatives, except in the cases noted in {{GHGpar|22|b}} and q. This points, however, not to an actual doubling, but merely to a strengthening of the consonant, giving more body to the monosyllabic stem, and making it approximate more to the character of triliteral forms.

The development of biliteral to triliteral stems ({{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}) generally takes place in the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} and 3rd ''plur. perfect Qal'' of ''transitive'' verbs, or at any rate of verbs expressing an activity, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סָבַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבוּ}}: {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}} (but with suffix {{GHGheb|text=חַנַּ֫נִי}}, ver. 11); sometimes with an evident distinction between transitive and intransitive forms, as {{GHGheb|text=צָרַר|translate=to make strait}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַר|translate=to be in a strait}}; see further details, including the exceptions, in aa. The development of the stem takes place (''a'') necessarily whenever the strengthening of the 2nd radical is required by the character of the form (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִלֵּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁדֵּד}}), and (''b'') as a rule, whenever the 2nd radical is followed or preceded by an essentially long vowel, as, in Qal, {{GHGheb|text=סָבוֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָבוּב}}, in Pôʿl and Pôʿal, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבַב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|b}}
'''2.''' The biliteral stem always (except in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}, see below) takes the vowel which would have been required between the ''second'' and ''third'' radical of the ordinary strong form, or which stood in the ground-form, since that vowel is characteristic of the form ({{GHGpar|43|b}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}} answering to {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מָּה}} to the ground-form ''qăṭălăt'', {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מּוּ}} to the ground-form ''qăṭălû''; {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹב}} to {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|c}}
'''3.''' The insertion of {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} (mentioned under a), for the purpose of strengthening the second radical, never takes place (see {{GHGpar|20|l}}) in the final consonant of the word, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹב}}, not {{GHGheb|text=תַּםּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹבּ}}; but it appears again on the addition of afformatives or suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּמּ֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹ֫בּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וּנִי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|d}}
'''4.''' When the afformative begins with a consonant ({{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}), and hence the strongly pronounced second radical would properly come at the end of a closed syllable, a ''separating vowel'' is inserted between the stem-syllable and the afformative. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}} this vowel is {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹנוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}} (for ''sabb-tā, sabb-nû, tasōbb-nā'').
